mod.name: QE SDK 0.24 Editor QA Scaffold
mod.author: HackHub Quest Editor
mod.description: Evidence-only project for SDK 0.24 in-game verification: native Wi-Fi, HTTP/curl events, the Timer node delay and calendar modes, and the Twotter node (accounts, backdated series, cleanup). Nothing auto-starts — claim one quest at a time with the harness command `qe24 run` — so a tester sees one row's noise, not five.

quests.name: QESdk024EditorQa
quests.title: QE SDK 0.24 editor QA
quests.description: Install on a throwaway save to verify editor-generated native Wi-Fi and SDK 0.24 HTTP/browser events. When this checklist says an objective ticks, look at the active quest/objective tracker: the line should become checked/completed, often with a debug toast.

mail.subject: QE24 editor QA scaffold
mail.content: Editor QA scaffold is active. Tick means the active quest/objective tracker line becomes checked/completed; the webpage loading by itself is not enough. Open http://qe24-website.test/ and /echo, then record which of http-request and http-response checked off. Connect to Wi-Fi QE24-LAB-5G with passphrase correct-horse-battery, then disconnect.

data.label: QE24 editor scaffold started; native Wi-Fi node emitted with bssid/channel/wps.
QE24 editor scaffold OnObjectivesStart/listeners registered or re-registered after load.

data.name: http-response
data.description: Open http://qe24-website.test/ and /echo in Browser. If this objective gets a checkmark/completed state, Http.Response fired for the editor website.
data.hint: Report: page loaded yes/no, http-response checked yes/no, and any debug toast/log text. If the page loads but this stays unchecked, record Response as not fired.
data.info: r166 evidence-only SDK 0.24 QA scaffold; no feature fence should be lifted from this project alone.

data.name: http-request
data.description: Open http://qe24-website.test/ and /echo in Browser. If this objective gets a checkmark/completed state, Http.Request fired before the response.
data.hint: Report: page loaded yes/no, http-request checked yes/no, and any debug toast/log text. It may differ from http-response; that is the point of this check.
data.info: r166 evidence-only SDK 0.24 QA scaffold; no feature fence should be lifted from this project alone.

data.name: http-intercepted
data.description: Optional: with the raw qe24 harness also installed, run qe24 intercept on, open http://qe24-website.test/, then qe24 intercept queue and qe24 intercept forward. Check whether this objective completes.
data.hint: Report held request yes/no and http-intercepted checked yes/no. Run qe24 intercept off if anything appears stuck.
data.info: r166 evidence-only SDK 0.24 QA scaffold; no feature fence should be lifted from this project alone.

quests.description: Auto-starts. Timer A (2 in-game minutes) must fire mail + toast. Timer B (2 in-game hours) must fire on reload survival, and must be cancelled if the quest is completed or abandoned first.

mail.content: The 2 in-game minute timer fired. S-01 (fire) is green if you read this within a few seconds of loading the save.

quests.name: QESdk024TimerCalQa
quests.title: Timer QA (calendar: S-05/S-06/S-07/S-13)
quests.description: Auto-starts. Two rows fire within seconds (an exact date already past, and a coming day already past today - both must fire immediately). The third arms a mixed '1 month 2 weeks 2 days at 18:23' row that resolves at arm time: read it with 'qe24 timers' instead of waiting. Save and reload before it is due - it must still be listed.

quests.name: QESdk024WaitMonthQa
quests.title: Timer QA (Wait in months: S-14, S-09)
quests.description: Auto-starts. First row: Wait 1 minute - fires a second later, so you know the chain ran. Second row: Wait 1 month - months have no field in the engine's duration form, so this is the scheduleAt path. Read it with 'qe24 timers'; on a day the next month has, it must land on the same day number one month on (that is S-09's claim as well).

mail.content: This is the engine's own duration form (schedule), the path S-01/S-02 verified. It arriving about a second after load is expected: one in-game minute is one real second at scale 60.

data.label: Now arming Wait 1 month (scheduleAt) - read 'qe24 timers'

mail.subject: Wait 1 month row fired now
mail.content: If this arrived without a month passing, the month Wait behaved like an instant one - that is a finding, please report it.

quests.name: QESdk024TwotterQa
quests.title: Twotter QA (T-08/T-09/T-10/T-11/T-13)
quests.description: Claim it with 'qe24 run tw1'. The moment it starts, the editor's Twotter node posts a series from @qe24_editor: five tweets, four backdated (a year, three months, six weeks, twelve days) and one that posts as you watch. Open Twotter and search qe24_editor: T-08 is the face and the counts, T-09 is the order and the ages. Then save and reload (T-10), and finally open the profile and one post so both objectives tick — the Complete button appears then, and pressing it is T-11: the account and its posts must disappear.
quests.closingObjectiveText: Twotter QA recorded — the series was on @qe24_editor.

data.label: Twotter QA started: @qe24_editor now carries the series. Open Twotter and search for it.

tweets.content: A year ago today this account was the only thing that worked. T-09 wants this row reading 'a year ago'.
Three months back: the manifest was sealed at 02:40 and nobody had signed for it.
Six weeks back: an attaché case on a bench, and nobody came back for it. (Six weeks, not a month — the age should read 'a month ago' only if the game rounds it there.)
Twelve days ago somebody asked the right question. We should not have ignored it.
This one posts the moment the quest runs, so it should read 'a few seconds ago'.

quests.name: QESdk024TwotterShareQa
quests.title: Twotter QA (T-12: two quests, one account)
quests.description: T-12, the rule Zeis approved. This quest posts from the SAME account as 'Twotter QA (T-08...)': @qe24_editor. Claim both with 'qe24 run tw1' and 'qe24 run tw2', then watch what each completion does. Finishing the first quest while the other is still live must leave the account standing; finishing the second must remove it, whichever order you complete them in. Read the state after each step with 'qe24 twotter audit'.

data.label: Second quest posting from @qe24_editor (T-12's shared account).

tweets.content: Posted by the second quest that shares this account - T-12 wants it on the same profile.

quests.name: QESdk024TwotterPostEventQa
quests.title: Twotter QA (T-13: does Twotter.Post ever fire?)
quests.description: Optional, and it never completes anything. The plan says the game's Twotter.Post event is about a quest's own DECLARED tweets — the path the editor refuses to use — so opening one of our API-posted tweets should fire PostSeen and not Post. Claim it with 'qe24 run tw3' before browsing, open a post, and look at the journal: the row ticking by itself is the finding. The r185 run already answered this (it stayed unchecked), so this quest is here to keep the question testable.

data.label: T-13 canary armed: open any Twotter post now and watch this quest's single objective.

data.name: post-event-canary
data.description: Expected to STAY unchecked: Twotter.Post is what the game fires for a quest's own declared tweets, and the editor does not emit those. If this row ever ticks by itself, say so — it changes what the manual may promise about When-event triggers.
data.hint: Nothing to press: the whole point is that it cannot be completed by hand either. Report only if it ticks.
data.info: r185/r186 Twotter QA. Row meaning: reference/sdk-0.24-qa/STATUS.md.
